r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/567-d1/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/567-d1/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from 567-d1 alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r8-fence-case.title: Fence case still answered; archive c4 still consistent
r8-fence-case.imperative: Confirm a fenced Commander's learning still reaches the Admiral under the new text, and that archive c4's deny-glob on .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md remains consistent with it.
r8-fence-case.finding: The fence case keeps an answer, and c4 stays consistent -- both EXECUTED, not read off the report. Learning route: a fenced Commander's episodes go to episodes/, a tracked path inside its own worktree, and the commit carries them out; the new delegated text states exactly that and the feedback gate's single postcondition (verify_episode_captured.py) is what proves it. The export route survives too: I ran the real evaluate_git_change_policy from scripts/checklist_engine.py over archive c4's actual policy and got .agent-work/staged-feedback/<work-id>/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md ALLOWED, .agent-work/staged-feedback/<work-id>/FENCE.md ALLOWED, .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md DENIED, .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.collected.json DENIED. The mechanism is _glob_match's basename fallback firing only for separator-free patterns, so the deny globs anchor at the root and cannot reach the nested staging dir. So 'stage it under .agent-work/staged-feedback/<work-id>/' and 'c4 deny-globs it out of your commit outright' are simultaneously true, and the two sides are symmetric: the Admiral text tells the Admiral to look in both places the delegated text tells the Commander to write.

r9-convention.title: Re-review convention vs what this run actually did
r9-convention.imperative: Judge the new skills/reviewer/SKILL.md paragraph against .agent-work/567-d1/g1b-review/ and g3-review/ round 1 and 2 files: does the written convention describe what actually worked?
r9-convention.finding: The convention's decisive claim is right and evidence-backed; one clause is narrower than the practice it was drawn from. CONFIRMED against this run: g1b review.json BLOCK (10 items, fails on r4-quality and r7-attack) then review-2.json APPROVE (12 items, override_reason None); g3 review.json BLOCK (7 items, fail on r3-evidence) then review-2.json APPROVE (7 items, override_reason None). Both rounds used a NEW file, left round 1 untouched, and consolidated APPROVE with NO override -- which is precisely the implementer's argument for why the re-consolidate-with-override-reason shape is the wrong one, since re-driving the old file would have forced either a fail-to-pass downgrade or an override written for a finding that was fixed. The issue named two shapes and the written convention picks the one the evidence supports, with the reason stated. GAP (non-blocking, worth the Commander's eye): 'Add this round's rechecks with append, one flat sibling per finding the previous round raised' does not describe either round. g3 round 2 appended NOTHING and re-ran base check r3-evidence in the fresh file; g1b round 2 appended FIVE siblings against TWO prior findings. The practice is actually: a finding that maps onto a base check is rechecked there, because the new file's base checks are fresh and pending, so recording pass is not a downgrade; a finding with no base-check home gets an appended sibling. As written the clause over-prescribes -- following it literally yields a redundant sibling beside an already-fresh base check. Harmless in effect, and the append-is-a-sibling mechanics it teaches are correct and needed (I relied on them to append r7-r10 here), so this is incomplete prose, not a false model.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. Both dispositions are backed by evidence that reproduces independently, and every negative survives a widened re-run with a positive control. #596's crux is confirmed at source: the feedback gate has exactly one postcondition (verify_episode_captured.py) and no export check, so the old commander-delegated clause was false as written; the repair replaces it with the measured fact, reinvents no successor playbook (checked against ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT's hard bound and verify_retirement.py's RETIRED_NAMES), leaves the fence case answered via committed episodes, and stays consistent with archive c4 -- which I proved by running the real evaluate_git_change_policy, not by reading the report. #526's 'does not reproduce, and never did in the skill corpus' holds against 1792 revisions on all refs, widened past the implementer's own greps to the overlay and .baseline mirrors; the 16-of-17 command-check census reproduces exactly; the survey-reuse negative holds corpus-wide against the pre-change tree. Scope is clean, all three template copies are byte-identical, and the census delta is 1:1 with nothing dropped. Two non-blocking observations recorded: the new re-review convention's 'one flat sibling per finding' clause describes neither round this run actually ran, and the doctrine-vs-spine coupling that caused #596 is uncorrected (triage candidate raised).

triage_candidates.statement: Doctrine prose asserts facts owned by COMMANDER_SPINE.template.json with nothing tying the two together. #596 happened because three doctrine sites claimed the feedback gate enforced an export it never checked. This gate corrected all three by hand, but the coupling is unchanged: if the spine's postcondition set moves again, skills/commander-delegated/SKILL.md, skills/admiral/SKILL.md and skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md go stale silently, and the approval census makes the fan-out five files rather than three. Out of scope here -- the fix is tooling or a docs/agents rule, and docs/agents promotion is the human's call.
